sentences.text:
Mr. Satyendra Singh Rajput - Advocate for the appellan
 Mr. Alok Sharma - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.
The appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A.No. 6368 of 2024, first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

The appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 374 (2) of the Cr.P.C. against the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 13.03.2024 passed by Forth Additional Sessions Judge, Guna (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No. 202/2021 whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced under Section 376(2)(L), 323 and 450 of IPC to undergo maximum rigorous imprisonment of ten years with maximum fine of Rs. 2,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Court below has wrongly convicted the appellant ignoring the evidence of prosecutrix/(PW/1) as well as son of prosecutrix/(PW/3).
It is further argued that there is material contradiction in the statements of PW/1 and PW/3 in respect to place of incident as well as other material particulars.
As per prosecutrix who is a major married woman at the time of incident she was sleeping inside the room and the door was bolted inside the room.
It is not the case of prosecution that appellant broke the gate and opened it as described by the prosecutrix at para 5.

PW/3 entirely changed the versions of the prosecution story at para 2 to 4 wherein, he stated that the incident occurred in their shop which was opened at the time of incident and there was some fight between his mother and the appellant and thereafter FIR was lodged.
At the most it is the case of consensual sexual relationship, therefore, DNA report looses its significance.
It is further argued that appellant has already served 7 months incarceration out of the total jail sentence awarded.
The appeal is likely to take long time to come up for final hearing and the appellant has hope and believe that he would succeed.
Hence, he prayed to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant looking to the short period of jail sentence.
On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the application and prayed for rejection of the same.

sentences.text: Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, application (I.A. No. 6368 of 2024) is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
He is further directed to mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 23.10.2024 and on subsequent dates as may be given in this regard.
List the case in due course.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.

Certified copy/ e-copy as per rules/directions.
(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (LJ*)
